title: Why Costco never raises the $1.50 hot dog

hook.a: Costco makes half its profit before you buy anything.
hook.b: Why does Costco's hot dog still cost what it did in 1985?

numbers.label: Operating income FY2026 and membership share
numbers.status: verified (primary); ratio computed from primary figures
numbers.formula: 50.6% = $5,907M membership fees / $11,685M operating income. 1 renewal point = 1% x $5,907M = ~$59M. Scenarios: fees(t+1) = fees(t) x r + N, base $5,907M, r = 89.8% worldwide renewal (fees are worldwide), N = $5,907M x (1 - 0.898) = ~$602M of new-member fees a year held flat. At r = 85.8% (-4 pts) year-5 fees = $5,017M, i.e. -$890M = 7.6% of operating income; -7 pts: -$1,468M = 12.6%. Assumes fee revenue drops through at ~100% margin and ignores fee increases and upgrades.

analysis.title: What happens to Costco's profit if renewals slip
analysis.finding: Membership fees ($5.9B) are ~50.6% of operating income, so every point of renewal rate is worth ~$59M a year on day one and compounds if lower renewal persists. At -4 pts of renewal, fee revenue ends year 5 about $890M lower (7.6% of today's operating income).
